descriptionChirho: A Hebrew feminine noun (מַחֲצִית) meaning 'half, one half of a whole', used in both construct state ('half of') and with pronominal suffixes ('half of it'). Attested in contexts of census tax (half a shekel, Exod 30:13,15), tribal land divisions (Josh 21:25; 1 Chr 6:55), and proportional measures. Multilingual signatures are uniform: eng 'half/half-of-it', spa 'mitad/su-mitad', arb 'نِصْف/نِصْفَهَا', kor '절반/반', swa 'nusu/nusu-yake', hin 'आधा/आधा-उसका'. The suffixed forms (S110953) are grammatical inflections of the same lexical sense as the construct forms (S110950).
